title: context-cards-and-exec-summaries
content:
Purpose: fast reference 'cue cards' for ideas I want to try this quarter. Not polished — brain-dump style.

High-level themes I care about
- Make KV cache eviction more workload-aware (not just LRU). Tune for long-tail doc reads and interactive sessions.
- Combine lightweight prefix compression with selective decompression to save memory on long-context customer sessions.
- Eval that isolates hallucination amplification when we quantize or evict context.
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: small batching + aggressive cache hits beats large batches for interactive UI SLOs.

Paper / blog quick summaries (one-liners + why it matters)
1) "Adaptive KV Eviction for Mixed Workloads" (arXiv 2801.01234)
- What: proposes a hybrid eviction policy that blends LRU with semantic reuse score computed from token overlap and retrieval signals.
- Key idea: predict reuse probability from small sketch of last k tokens + retrieval context; demote rarely-used entries even if recently accessed.
- Why it matters: could reduce cold-cache token re-computation in multi-session workloads (chat + background indexing).
- Immediate thought: implement offline replay on our request logs to compute reuse score distribution. Add features: session age, retrieval-score, user-id frequency.

2) "Sparse Prefix Compression for Long Contexts" (conf talk notes)
- What: compress prefixes with low-information content into compact summaries and restore full tokens on demand. Uses a small transformer to reconstruct only when needed.
- Key idea: store compressed prefix + checksum; if a predicted 'reconstruction need' is low, skip decompression for generation.
- Why: big win on GPU memory for very long sessions ( > 50k tokens ) where most of the prefix is stale or redundant.
- Risk: reconstruction errors can change model outputs. Need a fidelity probe.

3) "Micro-batching for Conversational SLOs" (engineering blog)
- What: trade off between per-request latency and GPU throughput by batching for 10-20ms windows (micro-batches) rather than waiting for large batches.
- Why: practical for hosted API where tail latency matters. Sharp reduction in P99 when combined with priority scheduling.
- Integration idea: expose micro-batch window as a per-route config in Redwood Console; tie to SLO and cost model.

4) "Quantization-induced Hallucination Modes" (poster)
- What: quantization can subtly shift logits leading to repeat hallucination types on low-temp decoding. Some hallucinations are amplified when past context is fuzzy.
- Why: explains why some customers see worse factuality after we enable 4-bit for their model.
- Action: add a lightweight hallucination detector regression to Optimize pipeline; flag dramatic shifts post-quantization rollout.

Notes-to-self: experiments to prioritize
- Offline: run 'reuse-scoring' replay on last 30 days of host-api logs (sample 1M requests) — compute correlation between reuse score and latency cost. Hypothesis: reuse score better predictor than recency alone. (owner: me)
- Small-scale: implement a toy prefix-compression layer in the private runtime branch; run fidelity probe with our eval set (100 prompts per customer). (owner: Mira)
- Canary: add micro-batch window config to one low-traffic route; measure P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec. (owner: Evan)
- Safety/regression: craft probes that target common hallucination templates and run before/after quantization on each variant. (owner: me + safety)

Practical constraints and guardrails
- Observability: need token-level attribution to see whether missing prefix tokens caused hallucination — telemetry gap today. File ticket JIRA-ENG-4123.
- Storage: compressed prefixes complicate snapshotting for Dedicated; ensure on-disk format is recoverable for restarts.
- Privacy: compressed prefix must not allow easier reconstruction of sensitive tokens. Add KMS tagging requirement for compressed blobs.

Quick TODOs (next 2 weeks)
- [ ] Spin up a replay job and compute reuse-score features (ask infra for 2x CPU nodes).
- [ ] Draft a short design doc for prefix-compression (one A4) to share with applied-ml and runtime.
- [ ] Add micro-batch flag to dev branch and test with local perf harness.
- [ ] Create eval prompt set for hallucination regression (pull from existing Optimize probes, ~300 examples).
- [ ] Slack post summarizing tradeoffs and ask for volunteers to pair on experiments.

Open questions / unknowns
- How often will compressed prefix reconstruction be triggered in real traffic? If >5% the net win might vanish. Need realistic sampling.
- Can reuse-score be computed cheaply enough at runtime? If not, need model distillation or sketching.
- What's the user-visible failure mode for wrong decompression? Silent drift vs obvious hallucination?

Scratch ideas (wildcards)
- 'Lazy materialization' where we only decompress prefix fragments around current attention window instead of full prefix.
- 'Eviction hints' surfaced in SDK: product can mark conversation spans as 'important' to avoid eviction. Simple UI flag for customers.
- 'Probabilistic prefix' — keep multiple compressed variants and pick reconstruction strategy based on query. Probably too heavy but interesting.

References and quick links
- Replay dataset / sample code: internal branch -> runtime/replay/priya-reuse (see PR referenced above).
- Slack convo: #runtime-kv-eviction thread (link in linked_artifacts).
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4123 (telemetry)

End-of-note. Will refine into two follow-up artifacts: 1) one-pager design for prefix-compression; 2) experiment plan for reuse-scoring replay.

Notes stamped: Priya (2028-04-02) — leaving as working doc.
